Definition: from G1537 and G138; actively, to tear out; middle voice, to select; figuratively, to release:--deliver, pluck out, rescue.
BiblicalUsage: exairéō is the word for deliver, pluck out, rescue. In Matthew 5:29, the text says "pluck it out." In Matthew 18:9, the text says "pluck it out."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, exairéō is a reminder that God really does deliver; escape is not luck, it is His hand at work. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
